split.description:
Michael Doyle was one of the Irish coal miners hanged as a Molly Maguire in the Pennsylvania anthracite region. He was tried at Mauch Chunk in Carbon County for the murder of the mine boss John P. Jones, in prosecutions driven by the Reading Railroad president Franklin B. Gowen — who acted as a private prosecutor against the union he was trying to destroy, using evidence gathered by the Pinkerton agent James McParland. Doyle was hanged at the Carbon County Prison on June 21, 1877, one of ten men executed in Pennsylvania that day.

This record previously carried a second case and a second life. It had been conflated with Father Michael Doyle, the Camden 28 priest, who is a separate record in this database and who died in 2022.
